title: Choose piDeck’s visual world
question: How should a solo developer see and control a large live agent fleet?

options.label: Broadcast Multiview
options.lineage: live broadcast control rooms and vision mixers
options.thesis: The fleet is a live program: every agent has a feed, attention has a tally, and interventions happen from one control surface.
options.viewport: A compact supervisor rail frames a wall of live agent feeds; the selected run expands into a central program monitor while an intervention desk remains anchored below.
options.risk: A literal wall of equal tiles would become surveillance noise, so feed scale must follow urgency and workflow hierarchy.

raised.raise: Every critical state changes shape and label as well as color.
Paused and deferred work remains spatially reachable instead of disappearing into filters.
Responsive layouts preserve whole agent-feed units rather than compressing them into illegibility.
Each alert exposes the single next safe decision, and rerouting updates immediately.
Intervention state is explicit, replayable, and linked back to the event that caused it.
Nested workflow depth is structural and unmistakable, never decorative indentation.

options.label: Flight Progress Bay
options.lineage: air-traffic flight-progress strips and controller bays
options.thesis: Each agent run is a physical strip moving through a shared bay; exceptions get pulled forward and every handoff leaves a mark.
options.viewport: A fleet-wide strip bay dominates the screen, grouped by supervisor and workflow, with an attention rack above and a selected run’s event record opening beside it.
options.risk: It is a familiar operations metaphor and can collapse into rows of tiny cards if the strip grammar is not enforced.

options.label: Terminal Wayfinding
options.thesis: The interface routes the operator from fleet overview to the next consequential decision with uncompromising signage.
options.viewport: A monumental attention band names the fleet’s next decision while supervisor corridors and agent destinations recede beneath it with time-to-impact labels.
options.case: It wins immediate action clarity, but identifies less strongly with a developer managing concurrent technical work.
options.risk: A one-decision-at-a-time system can hide useful peripheral awareness during a large incident.

options.label: Arcade Fleet Grid
options.thesis: Agents become strict tile-bound actors with unmistakable sprite states.
options.viewport: A tile-grid fleet stage ranks active agents beneath a compact score rail.
options.case: The state grammar is excellent, but the game frame weakens trust and reduces complex work to characters.
options.kept: Critical states now obey shape, label, and palette laws.
options.risk: Large-fleet supervision would read as gamified rather than operational.

options.label: Cutting Bench
options.lineage: film workprints, perforated rails, and pinned trims
options.thesis: Agent execution becomes a scrubbable workprint where stopped and deferred moments remain pinned in view.
options.viewport: A perforated event rail crosses the screen with intervention moments flagged and paused runs hanging below.
options.case: It explains one run beautifully but cannot carry a large simultaneous fleet as clearly as the multiview.
options.kept: Deferred and paused work remains spatially reachable.
options.risk: The linear rail overstates sequence and understates concurrency.

options.label: Character Catalog
options.thesis: A finite agent roster reflows as stable whole cells with distinct identities.
options.viewport: A ranked pastel roster fills the screen with one personality-led cell per agent.
options.case: The roster remains legible, but anthropomorphism obscures work state and intervention consequence.
options.kept: Responsive layouts preserve whole feed units.
options.risk: It makes consequential approvals feel collectible and unserious.

options.label: Recoverable Fold
options.thesis: Every workflow exposes its current transformation and every intervention remains recoverable.
options.viewport: One workflow’s state graph unfolds as a precise crease diagram beside its current execution form.
options.case: It communicates state lineage but cannot provide fast fleet-wide comparison.
options.kept: Every intervention links back to a recoverable event state.
options.risk: The continuous-sheet metaphor breaks across independent supervisors and failures.

options.label: Cloud Quarry
options.thesis: Nested workflows become atmospheric blocks whose density exposes operational weight.
options.viewport: A sectional fleet landscape stacks workflow blocks around deep blue structural gaps.
options.case: The depth is memorable, but abstract mass conceals precise status and safe controls.
options.kept: Nested workflow depth becomes structural rather than decorative.
options.risk: Atmosphere would compete directly with operational certainty.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished dark developer dashboard with sidebar navigation, KPI cards, an activity feed, and a chat-style run inspector.
canonCard.viewport: A left sidebar and top metrics frame a center fleet table with a right-hand event inspector.
canonCard.risk: Immediately usable but visually and structurally indistinguishable from generic AI operations tools.
